harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across the three-node AlmaLinux 9 cluster: node1 initialized as primary, node2 and node3 cloned via pg_basebackup as async standbys (firewalld opened for the postgresql service; replication role/credentials generated on-node and rotated after an accidental partial exposure in a debug echo). Demonstrated failover by writing a final transaction, stopping PostgreSQL on node1 (simulated primary loss), confirming zero data loss on both standbys, promoting node2 with pg_ctl promote, repointing node3 to follow node2, and rejoining node1 as a fresh standby of node2 via pg_basebackup. Final topology: node2 primary, node1 and node3 standbys, all data consistent. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and health on all three nodes, rebooted them one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled each until reachable, and proved a changed boot_id plus recovered PostgreSQL role/replication/data (row count 7) after each restart, always keeping at least one other node up as an independent recovery path.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 16.14 via dnf module postgresql:16 on node1, node2, node3
Added CLUSTER_HOSTS to /etc/hosts on all nodes and set up cluster SSH keys
Initialized primary DB on node1 (postgresql-setup --initdb), configured wal_level/max_wal_senders/hot_standby and pg_hba.conf for replication
Opened firewalld postgresql service on all three nodes (root cause of initial pg_basebackup 'no route to host')

Generated a replicator role/password on node1; password briefly leaked into a debug sed output and was rotated twice, then propagated via scp to /root/.pgrepl_pass (0600) and injected into primary_conninfo via Python file edits with no argv/stdout exposure
Created appdb.ledger table with baseline rows on node1
Cloned node2 and node3 as standbys via pg_basebackup -R against node1; verified pg_stat_replication and data parity
Simulated primary loss: final committed write on node1, confirmed both standbys fully caught up (WAL receive=replay), stopped postgresql on node1
Promoted node2 to primary with pg_ctl promote; verified pg_is_in_recovery=false and no data loss, wrote a post-promotion row
Repointed node3's primary_conninfo to node2; verified streaming and data parity
Rejoined node1 as a standby of node2 via fresh pg_basebackup -R (its old primary timeline made in-place restart unsuitable); verified streaming and full data set
Captured boot_id + service/replication health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially via systemctl reboot (one at a time), polling each until reachable, verifying changed boot_id and recovered PostgreSQL role/replication/row count each time

evidence.requirement: Primary/standby topology installed and streaming (node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys)
evidence.summary: node1 started as primary, replicator role created, node2/node3 cloned via pg_basebackup and confirmed streaming in pg_stat_replication with matching ledger data

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline before disruption, including a final pre-outage committed write and standby catch-up confirmation
evidence.summary: Wrote 'last-committed-before-outage' row on node1 and confirmed both node2 and node3 had received/replayed that WAL LSN before the outage

evidence.requirement: Primary loss simulated and standby promoted to writable primary without losing committed data
evidence.summary: Stopped postgresql on node1 (primary loss), promoted node2 with pg_ctl promote, verified pg_is_in_recovery=false and all 5 pre-outage rows present plus a new post-promotion write

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary rejoins as standby of the new primary; surviving standby also follows new primary
evidence.summary: node3 repointed to node2 and caught up; node1 rebuilt via pg_basebackup from node2 and started as standby.signal-based standby; final cluster-wide write (id 38) confirmed present on both node1 and node3

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id c2ffc729...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node unreachable then boot_id changed to 31dcade0...; postgresql active, standby recovery mode, 7 rows intact

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/quorum
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d6298ced...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable then boot_id changed to 2888cca7...; postgresql active as primary, 7 rows intact, both node1 and node3 reconnected as streaming standbys

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id c207ab79...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable then boot_id changed to 6b3540a2...; postgresql active, standby recovery mode, 7 rows intact; final cluster-wide check on node2 shows both standbys streaming and full data set
